title: PowerPoint: choose an OpenAI or Anthropic model when creating or editing with Copilot
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, provider controls and December 9 change are supported by Microsoft's documentation. Minor corrections should finish two control paths at their selection and qualify the general EU, EFTA and UK default alongside the newer-tenant apps-only exception.

claims.claim: Users can select Claude in Edit with Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: The Anthropic provider setting governs users' access to Claude in Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: When this setting is enabled and the All users for Microsoft 365 apps only option is selected, Claude models from Anthropic are available only in Copilot experiences in the following Microsoft 365 apps: Excel PowerPoint Word

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Claude models are enabled by default for most commercial cloud customers outside the EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: Microsoft enables Claude models on by default for most customers in commercial cloud (excluding EU/EFTA and UK).

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Regional default; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The general Claude provider default is No users in EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: the default is set to No users. These regions include the European Union (EU), the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and the United Kingdom (UK).
claims.fix: Qualify Scope: Regional default and controls[0].note: 'The general Claude provider page states No users for EU, EFTA and UK; the apps-only page states that All users for Microsoft 365 apps only is enabled by default for tenants in those regions created after March 25, 2026.' The exception is already described in What's changing. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/copilot-anthropic-apps.

claims.claim: OpenAI-operated models are enabled for all users of eligible commercial customers unless No users is selected.
claims.quote: OpenAI operated models are enabled for all users for eligible commercial customers, unless you specifically disable the use of OpenAI operated models by selecting No users

claims.claim: The OpenAI-operated models default took effect as of July 24, 2026.
claims.quote: As of July 24, 2026, OpenAI operated models are enabled for all users for eligible commercial customers

claims.claim: Selecting No users disables use of OpenAI-operated models.
claims.quote: Under Choose which users can access OpenAI operated models, select No users, and then select Save. After you disable OpenAI as a subprocessor, users won't have the option to use OpenAI operated AI models.

claims.claim: The apps-only Claude setting described here applies to customers in the EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: The information in this article applies only to customer in the European Union (EU), European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and United Kingdom (UK).

claims.claim: All users for Microsoft 365 apps only is withdrawn starting December 9, 2026.
claims.quote: There are important setting changes taking effect on December 9, 2026, including the following: The All users for Microsoft 365 apps only option will no longer be available.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricting provider access to specific users or groups permits only those users or group members to use features that rely on that provider.
claims.quote: When access is restricted by user or group assignment, only the specified users or group members can use Copilot features that rely on that AI provider.

claims.claim: Microsoft points to a Message center message sent November 9, 2026.
claims.quote: look for a message that was sent on November 9, 2026

claims.quote: with a title that starts with "Action may be required: Claude models in Microsoft Copilot."

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Choosing Claude means Anthropic processes content as a Microsoft subprocessor.
claims.quote: Anthropic has onboarded as a Microsoft subprocessor. As a subprocessor, Anthropic operates with Microsoft oversight through contractual safeguards and appropriate technical and organizational measures.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Using Claude in PowerPoint entails processing presentation content and prompts by Anthropic.
claims.quote: When Claude models from Anthropic are used in Copilot experiences in Excel, PowerPoint, or Word, data processing for these models occurs outside of the EU Data Boundary.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Claude processing is currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary

claims.claim: Claude models are excluded from in-country processing commitments where applicable.
claims.quote: currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Claude models are coming into the EU Data Boundary starting in December 2026.
claims.quote: Claude models from Anthropic are coming into the EU Data Boundary starting in December 2026.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention store data at Anthropic under Anthropic's own terms.
claims.quote: This means data is stored by Anthropic and not subject to your Microsoft Customer Agreement including commitments in the Product Terms and DPA. In this scenario, Anthropic acts as an independent processor

claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default for all scenarios.
claims.quote: Anthropic models with Data Retention (such as Fable 5.0) have additional controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center and are off by default for all scenarios

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Anthropic models with Data Retention require a separate explicit tenant-admin opt-in.
claims.quote: No users will have access to these models until the tenant admin explicitly opts in to enable use of Anthropic models with Data Retention.

claims.claim: OpenAI-operated models are excluded from applicable in-country processing commitments.
claims.quote: OpenAI models delivered through OpenAI as a subprocessor in Copilot experiences are currently excluded from in-country processing commitments when applicable.

claims.claim: OpenAI-operated models are included in the EU Data Boundary subject to the exceptions in Microsoft's EU Data Boundary documentation.
claims.quote: OpenAI operated models are included in the EU Data Boundary, except as otherwise noted in the EU Data Boundary documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a model choice for create and edit, rather than describing additional actions.
claims.quote: When create or edit a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint, you can now select which model to use, including both Open AI and Anthropic models.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that some features require Claude models to be enabled.
claims.quote: Some features are only available when Claude models are enabled. If you turn off Anthropic as a subprocessor, certain features may no longer be accessible.

claims.claim: Claude models are unavailable to federal GCC customers and all GCC High and DoD customers.
claims.quote: Claude models aren't available for federal customers in GCC or for any customers in GCC High and Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: OpenAI-operated models are not currently available in government or sovereign clouds.
claims.quote: Access to OpenAI operated models isn't currently available for use in government clouds (GCC, GCC High, DoD) or sovereign clouds.

claims.claim: The OpenAI provider setting affects only OpenAI-operated models; Microsoft-operated Azure OpenAI models remain available regardless of its value.
claims.quote: It controls only whether OpenAI models operated by OpenAI (provided by OpenAI as a subprocessor) can be used. OpenAI models operated by Microsoft (Azure OpenAI) aren't affected and remain available in Copilot regardless of this setting.
